pl-l4d32c4-d1e115.summary: States that times must be observed not only in carnal work but in celebrating weddings: they should not be celebrated from Septuagesima to the octave of Easter, three weeks before St. John's feast, or from Advent until after Epiphany; if done, they are to be separated.
claims: Weddings are forbidden in certain seasons.

pl-l4d32c4-d1e121.summary: Adds Pope Nicholas: I do not think one can in any way take a wife or celebrate marriages in Lent.
claims: Weddings are not to be held in Lent.

pl-l4d32c4.summary: Times must be observed not only for carnal union but for celebrating weddings: they are not to be held from Septuagesima to the octave of Easter, three weeks before St. John's feast, and from Advent until after Epiphany, on pain of separation; Pope Nicholas holds that no one may marry in Lent.
claims: Weddings are forbidden in Lent, Advent, and certain other seasons.
